evidence.quote: The most merciful thing in the world, I think, is the inability of the human mind to correlate all its contents. We live on a placid island of ignorance in the midst of black seas of infinity, and it was not meant that we should voyage far. The sciences, each straining in its own direction, have hitherto harmed us little; but some day the piecing together of dissociated knowledge will open up such terrifying vistas of reality
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator explains a premise that piecing together separated pieces of scientific knowledge will reveal terrifying realities.

evidence.quote: That glimpse, like all dread glimpses of truth, flashed out from an accidental piecing together of separated things/u2014in this case an old newspaper item and the notes of a dead professor.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator describes arriving at his conclusion by correlating separate documents.

evidence.quote: He questioned the sculptor with scientific minuteness; and studied with almost frantic intensity the bas-relief on which the youth had found himself working
evidence.paraphrase: Professor Angell interrogates the sculptor methodically and studies the artifact intensively.

evidence.quote: My uncle, it seems, had quickly instituted a prodigiously far-flung body of inquiries amongst nearly all the friends whom he could question without impertinence, asking for nightly reports of their dreams, and the dates of any notable visions for some time past.
evidence.paraphrase: The professor conducts a wide survey collecting people's dream reports and dates.

evidence.quote: There then followed an exhaustive comparison of details, and a moment of really awed silence when both detective and scientist agreed on the virtual identity of the phrase common to two hellish rituals so many worlds of distance apart.
evidence.paraphrase: The detective and scientist systematically compare ritual phrases and find them identical across distant cultures.

evidence.quote: the soapy, greenish-black stone with its golden or iridescent flecks and striations resembled nothing familiar to geology or mineralogy
evidence.paraphrase: The statuette's stone material is described as matching nothing known to geology or mineralogy.

evidence.quote: They worshiped, so they said, the Great Old Ones who lived ages before there were any men, and who came to the young world out of the sky. Those Old Ones were gone now, inside the earth and under the sea; but their dead bodies had told their secrets in dreams to the first man, who formed a cult which had never died.
evidence.paraphrase: The cult's account explains the Great Old Ones as beings who came from the sky before humanity and communicate through dreams.

evidence.quote: These Great Old Ones, Castro continued, were not composed altogether of flesh and blood. They had shape/u2014for did not this star-fashioned image prove it?/u2014but that shape was not made of matter. When the stars were right, They could plunge from world to world through the sky; but when the stars were wrong, They could not live.
evidence.paraphrase: Castro explains the physical nature of the Old Ones and how their viability depends on stellar alignment.

evidence.quote: They all lay in stone houses in Their great city of R'lyeh, preserved by the spells of mighty Cthulhu for a glorious resurrection when the stars and the earth might once more be ready for Them.
evidence.paraphrase: The Old Ones lie preserved across vast time in R'lyeh awaiting a future resurrection.

evidence.quote: The time would be easy to know, for then mankind would have become as the Great Old Ones; free and wild and beyond good and evil, with laws and morals thrown aside and all men shouting and killing and reveling in joy.
evidence.paraphrase: A projected future in which humanity, upon the Old Ones' return, abandons all morality in violent ecstasy.

evidence.quote: The great stone city R'lyeh, with its monoliths and sepulchers, had sunk beneath the waves; and the deep waters, full of the one primal mystery through which not even thought can pass, had cut off the spectral intercourse.
evidence.paraphrase: In the past the city R'lyeh sank beneath the sea, severing dream contact.

evidence.quote: in S. Latitude 47/u00b0 9', W. Longitude 126/u00b0 43' come upon a coastline of mingled mud, ooze, and weedy Cyclopean masonry which can be nothing less than the tangible substance of earth's supreme terror/u2014the nightmare corpse-city of R'lyeh, that was built in measureless eons behind history
evidence.paraphrase: The sailors encounter the risen ancient city R'lyeh at specific ocean coordinates.

evidence.quote: He had said that the geometry of the dream-place he saw was abnormal, non-Euclidean, and loathsomely redolent of spheres and dimensions apart from ours.
evidence.paraphrase: The city's geometry is described as non-Euclidean and belonging to dimensions apart from ours.

evidence.quote: twisted menace and suspense lurked leeringly in those crazily elusive angles of carven rock where a second glance showed concavity after the first showed convexity
evidence.paraphrase: The rock's angles behave contrary to ordinary spatial expectation, shifting between concave and convex.

evidence.quote: After vigintillions of years great Cthulhu was loose again, and ravening for delight.
evidence.paraphrase: The long-dormant entity Cthulhu is released into the world.

evidence.quote: Briden looked back and went mad, laughing shrilly as he kept on laughing at intervals till death found him one night in the cabin whilst Johansen was wandering deliriously.
evidence.paraphrase: A crew member goes insane and laughs until death after witnessing Cthulhu.

evidence.quote: I have looked upon all that the universe has to hold of horror, and even the skies of spring and the flowers of summer must ever afterward be poison to me.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator reports that his knowledge has permanently poisoned his perception of the world.

evidence.quote: what an age-old cult had failed to do by design, a band of innocent sailors had done by accident. After vigintillions of years great Cthulhu was loose again
evidence.paraphrase: The accidental awakening of Cthulhu represents a potential worldwide catastrophe.

evidence.quote: Now an unlettered seaman felt the same thing whilst gazing at the terrible reality.
evidence.paraphrase: An uneducated sailor independently perceives the same abnormal geometry described by the sculptor, corroborating its reality.

evidence.quote: What has risen may sink, and what has sunk may rise. Loathsomeness waits and dreams in the deep, and decay spreads over the tottering cities of men. A time will come
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator projects an inevitable future return of Cthulhu and decline of human civilization.
